content: Python Decimal pitfalls beyond 'use Decimal': constructing Decimal directly from a float literal (Decimal(0.1)) imports the float's binary imprecision - must construct from str or from an already-exact source; mixing a bare float into a Decimal expression re-introduces error and often raises TypeError inconsistently; comparing Decimal to float can silently coerce; must pick and document one rounding mode (e.g. ROUND_DOWN for conservative fills) explicitly rather than relying on the ambient default context, since Python's default Decimal context rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) is a global mutable that any imported library can alter.
